question: Why didn't the team just capture a start timestamp with Date.now() at module load and subtract it on each /health request?
reference_answer: They rejected that approach because it would require a module-scope binding that handle() doesn't have today, and because uptime derived from the wall clock can jump or go backwards if the system clock is adjusted; process.uptime() avoids reading the wall clock at all.

gold.heading_path: 0001: Report the Node process age as uptime, read per request from process.uptime() > Alternatives
gold.quote: Needs a module-scope binding in `src/server.js`, and wall-clock adjustment (manual clock set, NTP step) can make the reported uptime jump or go backwards.

gold.heading_path: 0003: Match GET /health as a third exact-match branch in handle, with no route table > Alternatives
